  CITY HALL COUNCIL CHAMBERS
  2200 HUNTINGTON DRIVE
  SAN MARINO, CA 91108

The City of San Marino appreciates your attendance. Citizens’ interest provides the Council
with valuable information regarding issues of the community.

Regular meetings are held on the 2nd Wednesday of every month at 6:00 p.m. Typically,
adjourned meetings are held on the last Friday of every month at 8:30 a.m.

In compliance with the Americans with Disabilities Act, any person with a disability who
requires a reasonable modification or accommodation in order to participate in a meeting
should contact the City Clerk via email at CityClerk@CityofSanMarino.org or by phone at
(626) 300­0705 prior to the meeting for assistance.

The public is welcome to attend the meeting in person or remotely via Zoom, however, the
meeting will proceed as normal even if there are technical difficulties with Zoom. The City will
do it’s best to resolve any technical issues as quickly as possible.

CALL TO ORDER

PLEDGE OF ALLEGIANCE

ROLL CALL

Council Member Chou, Council Member Lo, Council Member Shepherd Romey, Vice Mayor
Huang, and Mayor Talt

POSTING OF AGENDA

The agenda is posted 72 hours prior to each meeting at the following locations: City Hall,
2200 Huntington Drive, the Crowell Public Library, 1890 Huntington Drive, and the Stoneman
Building, 1560 Pasqualito Drive. The agenda is also posted on the City’s website:
http://www.cityofsanmarino.org.

PUBLIC COMMENTS

The City welcomes public input. Members of the public may address the City Council by
completing a public comment card and giving it to the City Clerk prior to the meeting. At this
time, the public may address the City Council on items that are not on the agenda. Pursuant
to state law, the City Council may not discuss or take action on issues not on the meeting
agenda (Government Code Section 54954.2). The Mayor reserves the right to place limits on
duration of comments. Staff may be asked to follow up on such items.

CITY MANAGER'S REPORT

This is an opportunity for the City Manager to inform the City Council and the public of any
upcoming events or matters of interest to the community.

MOTION TO WAIVE FURTHER READINGS

This action permits the City Council to act on ordinances and resolutions without having to
read the entire text of the ordinance or resolution. The title of an ordinance on First
Reading must be read in its entirety. An ordinance on Second Reading does not require
having the title read. However, the City Council may request that an ordinance or resolution
be read in its entirety before taking any action.

  PUBLIC HEARINGS

1.  PUBLIC HEARING AND CONSIDERATION OF RESOLUTION NO. R­23­
  12, A RESOLUTION RESCINDING RESOLUTION NO. R­21­14 AND
  APPROVING A MIXED USE PROJECT AT 2404 MISSION STREET AND
  FINDING THE APPROVAL CATEGORICALLY EXEMPT FROM CEQA
  PURSUANT TO GUIDELINES SECTION 15303 AND 15332
  Recommendation: Staff recommends the City Council conduct the public hearing, and
  consider adoption of the attached resolution rescinding the prior denial of the Project
  and approve Conditional Use Permit No. 20­05 and 20­16 and Design Review No. DRC
  20­29HP. If the City Council elects to adopt the resolution, an appropriate motion
  would be:“I move to adopt Resolution No. R­23­12, rescinding Resolution No. R­21­14
  and approving Conditional Use Permit Nos. 20­05 and 20­16 and Design Review No.
  DRC 20­29HP for the mixed use Project at 2404 Mission Street.”

  NEW BUSINESS

2.  ADOPTION OF RESOLUTION NO. R­23­09 CHANGING THE NAME
  FROM SAN MARINO CENTER TO SAN MARINO COMMUNITY CENTER
  Recommendation: Staff recommends the Council adopt Resolution No. R­23­09
  changing the name of the San Marino Center to “San Marino Community Center.” If
  the Council concurs with staff’s recommendations, an appropriate motion would be:
  “I move to adopt Resolution No. R­23­09, a Resolution of the City Council of the City
  of San Marino, California changing the name of the San Marino Center to “San Marino
  Community Center.”

  CONSENT CALENDAR

  Disbursements Report for the month of March 2023. If the City Council concurs with
  staff’s recommendation, an appropriate motion would be: “I move to receive and file
  the Monthly Disbursements Report for the month of March 2023.”

  Recommendation: Staff recommends the Council receive and file this report. If the
  City Council concurs with staff’s recommendation, an appropriate motion would be: “I
  move to receive and file the Cash and Investment Report for the Month of February
  2023.”

5.  APPROVAL OF MINUTES
  Recommendation: Staff recommends the Council approve the March 2023 minutes. If
  the City Council concurs with staff’s recommendation, an appropriate motion would
  be: “I move to approve the minutes of the special meeting of March 8, 2023, the
  regular meeting of March 8, 2023, the adjourned regular meeting of March 24, 2023,
  and the adjourned regular meeting of March 31, 2023.”

6.  ADOPTION OF RESOLUTION NO. R­23­11, APPOINTMENT OF PLAN
  ADMINISTRATORS FOR THE CITY OF SAN MARINO RETIREE
  HEALTH SAVINGS PLAN (RHS PLAN)
  Recommendation: Staff recommends the Council adopt Resolution No. R­23­11,
  Appointment of Plan Administrators for the City of San Marino Retiree Health Savings
  Plan (RHS Plan). If Council concurs, an appropriate motion would be: “I move to
  adopt Resolution No. R­23­11, Appointment of Plan Administrators for the City of San
  Marino Retiree Health Savings Plan (RHS Plan).”

7.  APPROVAL OF A REQUEST TO WAIVE THE SPECIAL EVENT PERMIT
  FEES FOR 4TH OF JULY COMMUNITY PARTNER EVENTS
  Recommendation: Staff recommends that the City Council waive the Special Event
  Permit fees associated with the 4th of July Pavilion, 4th of July Parade, and the JP
  Blecksmith Run. If the City Council agrees with staff’s recommendation, an
  appropriate motion would be: “I move to waive the Special Event Permit fees, City
  space rental fees, and staff time fees associated with the 4th of July Pavilion, 4th of
  July Parade, and the JP Blecksmith Run.”

  Friends of the Crowell Public Library 65 Year Celebration.”

9.  AUTHORIZATION TO DISPOSE OF SURPLUS PROPERTY BY PUBLIC
  AUCTION PER MUNICIPAL CODE SECTION 2.06.06
  Recommendation: Staff recommends the City Council approve the disposal of surplus
  vehicles and equipment via public auction pursuant to Municipal Code Section
  2.06.06. If the Council concurs, an appropriate motion would be: “I move to approve
  the disposal of surplus vehicles and equipment as listed in the staff report via public
  auction, pursuant to Municipal Code Section 2.06.06.”

10.  APPROVAL OF AGREEMENT AMENDMENT NO. 1 WITH DYNAMIC
  BUILDING MAINTENANCE FOR PROFESSIONAL MAINTENANCE
  SERVICES EXTENDING THE TERM THROUGH APRIL 30, 2024.
  Recommendation: Staff recommends the City Council approve Amendment No. 1 to
  the agreement with Dynamic Building Maintenance, and authorize the Acting City
  Manager to execute the amendment on behalf of the City. If Council concurs an
  appropriate motion would be:“I move to approve Amendment No. 1 to the
  Professional Maintenance Services Agreement with Dynamic Building Maintenance,
  extending the term through April 30, 2024, and authorize the Acting City Manager to
  execute the amendment on behalf of the City.”

11.  ADOPTION OF RESOLUTION NO. R­23­13 REDUCING THE HIRING
  AGE TO 16 FOR ENTRY LEVEL RECREATIONAL PART­TIME STAFF
  Recommendation: Staff recommends the Council adopt Resolution No. R­23­13
  lowering the hiring age to 16 for Lifeguards, Water Safety Instructors, and Program
  Leaders. If the City Council concurs with staff’s recommendation, an appropriate
  motion would be: “I move to adopt Resolution No. R­23­13, a Resolution of the City
  Council of the City of San Marino, California reducing the hiring age to 16 for
  Lifeguards, Water Safety Instructors, and Program Leaders.”

WRITTEN COMMUNICATIONS OR PUBLIC WRITINGS DISTRIBUTION

This is an opportunity to announce any written communications pertaining to the City
received by members of the City Council. All public writings distributed by the City of San
Marino to at least a majority of the City Council regarding any item on this agenda will be
made available at the Public Counter at City Hall located at 2200 Huntington Drive, San
Marino, California 91108, and will also be included in the public agenda packet that will
available for review at the City Council meeting.
